output.brief:
The wrong dates were not caused by the agency operators or the printer firmware. Printer records show the wrong shelf-life value (36 months instead of 24) arrived from PackBridge before any operator action. No overrides were made, and the printed text matched what was sent. Veltranol jobs through 3 Oct were correct, including those set up by agency operators after the firmware change. The first wrong job was 4 Oct. On 3 Oct Regulatory Affairs entered a 36-month value that should only take effect from 1 March 2027. PackBridge appears to have used it early. I am fairly sure of this chain, but we don't yet know why PackBridge ignored the valid-from date. The vendor's statement that it can't do this conflicts with the job records. The camera only checks print against the job, so it passed every faulty carton.

Do not warn or remove the agency operators. Do not switch off the camera check.

Do this now:
1. Fix the Veltranol shelf-life records so only the approved value can be read.
2. Hold every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct. This includes two lots from Line 1 now in the warehouse.
3. Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at each setup.
4. Check retained cartons of the two other products with future-dated edits, HX-15-30 and MR-05-14.
5. Ask Corvane to explain why the valid-from date was not honoured.

A 12-month site-wide reconciliation and over-labelling of other products are premature.
